newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - March 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - March 11.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- UK 'TO BEAT 2.5 PERCENT INFLATION GOAL'

Figures from the Office of National Statistics show that the annual rise in factory gate prices -- a key measure of UK inflation -- hit a 10 year low last month. Separately, Eddie George, governor of the Bank of England, has predicted retail price inflation (excluding mortgage interest payments) would fall below the government's target of 2.5 percent this year. The revelations represent a further easing of the pressure for an interest rate rise.
-- BUSINESS LEADERS ATTACK EXTREME EUROSCEPTICS

In a letter to the Financial Times, 23 business leaders -- including Sir Colin Marshall, president of the Confederation of British Industry (CBI) and chairman of British Airways -- have attacked 'the spread of extreme Euroscepticism' in the UK. While the authors deny the move is party political, it will inevitably be seen as a strong hint to the government over the increasingly Eurosceptical mood of the Tory party. The letter urges that whatever the differences over Emu, Britain should be united in its commitment to the single market.
-- FRANCE'S PLAN FOR OWN TIME ZONE SETS EU ALARMS RINGING

Transport ministers in the European Union are set to reject a plea from the French prime minister to end the practice of changing clocks by an hour between summer and winter. The French objection to switching to 'summer time' is based on practical and health concerns for farmers, children and old people. However, the transport ministers fear that a unilateral move by France on the issue would cause widespread disruption to transport schedules across the EU.
-- EMU 'D-DAY SCENARIO' PROVOKES SHUDDERS

The consensus among large companies in Europe is that any delay in the start of European economic and monetary union would probably be the death-knell for the project. With banks and institutions investing heavily in preparations for the January 1, 1999 start date, those involved in the project claim talk of a delay is politically motivated and ignores the potentially disastrous consequences such a move would entail.
-- CENTRICA 'UPFRONT' OVER DATABASE

Centrica, the demerged British Gas domestic supply business, has begun a nationwide mail shot of its 19 million UK customers, asking them whether they want to be sent information about additional services. The Centrica database is one of the largest in Europe, having cost the company more than 100 million stg to develop. The mailshot comes ahead of official guidance expected soon from the Data Protection Registrar, which last year expressed opposition to the use by regional electricity companies of their monopoly databases for unrelated services.
-- EMU DRIVE HITS CONSTRUCTION MACHINERY SALES

London-based consultancy Off-Highway Research has claimed that sales of construction machinery in western Europe will fall again in 1997, largely due to preparations by governments for economic and monetary union (Emu). The consultancy predicts that 1997 sales of machines such as dump trucks, excavators and wheeled loaders will fall 6 percent, after declining 7 percent in 1996. Off-Highway says government efforts to restrain public spending in order to meet Emu qualification targets is hitting state investment in construction, particularly in France and Germany.
-- SIEMENS TO SELL DEFENCE BUSINESS

German electrical and electronic group Siemens has announced plans to sell its defence electronics business just two weeks after telling staff it was seeking a joint venture partner for the business. Siemens has appointed US investment bank Morgan Stanley to draw up a shortlist of bidders for the business, which is dominated by Siemens Plessey in the UK. Potential bidders for the business include GEC of the UK, and ITT and Lockheed Martin of the US.
-- PSION TO LAUNCH NEW TECHNOLOGY

Psion, the UK company that manufactures handheld computers, has announced plans to launch two machines this year based on its next-generation 32-bit technology. One of both of the products is likely to be a highly sophisticated pocket PC capable of wireless digital communications. Details of the plans were announced as Psion reported a 38 percent increase in full-year pre-tax profits, to 16 million stg.
-- SOFTWARE DEMAND HELPS CMG RISE 37 PERCENT

Anglo-Dutch computer services group CMG has reported a 37 percent increase in underlying full year pre-tax profits, to 27.5 million stg. The company's performance, like that of others in the sector, was boosted by the trend to outsourcing and by preparations for the Millennium and for Emu. Turnover at CMG rose 25 percent, to 245.2 million stg.
-- PREMIER STANDS BY ALBANIAN OIL

UK oil independent Premier Oil has reported an 80 percent increase in 1996 net income, to 45.3 million stg. Announcing the results, Premier said the political upheaval in Albania would not alter its decision to step up its exploration drive. Premier expects annual spending on exploration and production is set to jump from 52 million stg to 80 million stg. Sales at Premier in 1996 rose 63 percent, to 138.8 million stg, while operating profits rose 85 percent to 76.1 million stg.
